purpose: Provide an executable fixture-local supplied propulsion response with explicit thrust direction, closure-ready application-point wrench and positive-consumption mass-flow semantics.

provenance.notes: The Scientific Authority accepted the fixture-local nonnegative thrust magnitude and unit body-direction profile, Closure-owned application-point transport, and nonnegative fuel-consumption sign. Legacy positive consumption is provenance only; product and Legacy runtime APIs are absent from the executable path.

expected_facts.claim: Independent 80-digit Decimal and C++17 implementations agree on thrust magnitude-direction composition, the closure-ready application-point force and intrinsic moment, and the resulting center-of-mass wrench consumer values.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Model, source, frame, clock, tick, revision, interval and quality identities are exact; finite physical values use the fixture-local absolute-plus-relative formula tolerance.

expected_facts.claim: A nonnegative fuel-consumption rate produces a negative mass delta over the same half-open interval, composes under interval partition and rejects a nonpositive candidate without a clamp.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Interval and mass-state identities are exact; duration, consumption, delta and candidate mass use the fixture-local formula tolerance.

expected_facts.claim: The executable rejects incompatible identity, invalid direction, negative physical magnitudes, non-finite values and depleted mass while detecting thrust reversal, pre-transported moment and mass-gain mutations.
expected_facts.tolerance_policy: Input rejection and mutation identities are exact; tolerance never repairs an invalid direction, sign, time interval or mass candidate.

acceptance: The bundle records explicit source/frame/time/configuration identity, formula inputs, force and moment intermediates, mass-flow integral and direct consumer results
The Python reference and C++17 probe share no implementation and neither imports product or Legacy code
Throttle/enable mapping, engine/fuel dynamics, dry-mass policy, canonical assets, configuration transitions and product contracts remain outside this slice
